candidates.title: Ancient Egypt Unveiled: Treasures from Egyptian Museums
candidates.blurb: Egyptian state museums loan antiquities to West Kowloon, testing how universal collections translate outside the Western museum circuit.

candidates.title: The Hong Kong Jockey Club Series: Treasures of the Mughal Court from the Victoria and Albert Museum
candidates.blurb: V&A Mughal holdings in dialogue with the Palace Museum's Qing collections, mapping parallel court aesthetics across empire.

candidates.title: Wonders of Imperial Carpets: Masterpieces from the Museum of Islamic Art, Doha
candidates.blurb: Doha lends Persian and Ottoman carpets to a museum whose DNA is Chinese imperial; cultural diplomacy via decorative arts.

candidates.title: A Movable Feast: The Culture of Food and Drink in China
candidates.blurb: Palace Museum objects read through culinary ritual and banquet structure, excavating the social life of imperial dining.

candidates.title: The Forbidden City and The Palace of Versailles: China-France Cultural Encounters in the Seventeenth and Eighteenth Centuries
candidates.blurb: Jesuit emissaries and court workshops as vectors of aesthetic exchange between Qing Beijing and Bourbon Paris.

candidates.title: Alicja Kwade: Waiting Pavilions
candidates.blurb: Kwade's mirrored pavilions occupy the former prison yard, inverting colonial architecture into percussive sculpture.

candidates.title: A History of China in Silk: The Chris Hall Collection at the Hong Kong Palace Museum
candidates.blurb: Private British collection of Chinese textiles re-contextualised in Hong Kong, mapping silk as historiography.

candidates.title: The Hong Kong Jockey Club Series: The Art of Armaments — Qing Dynasty Military Collection from The Palace Museum
candidates.blurb: Qing weaponry and ceremonial armour examined as aesthetic programme, beyond function into ornamental logic.

candidates.title: Proudly from Canton: The Muwen Tang Collection of Cantonese and Export Art
candidates.blurb: Export porcelain and trade paintings that refract Cantonese identity through the gaze of 18th-century European demand.

candidates.title: Fermata: Hong Kong in Venice
candidates.blurb: Collateral pavilion documentation from the 61st Venice Biennale, showing Hong Kong's negotiation of a global art stage.

candidates.title: Live: Hong Kong Art Exhibition
candidates.blurb: Survey of local contemporary practice, framing Hong Kong art through institutional rather than market definitions.

candidates.title: Tai Kwun Neon Connection
candidates.blurb: Commissioned neon works activate the heritage site's alleyways, indexing a disappearing urban typology through new production.
